title: Bedrock Spend Controls threat model
asset: The Bedrock bill, bounded per identity, tenant, or workload; correct usage attribution; enforcement within the documented bound (metering lag + min(lease remainder, deny propagation)); authorized and audited administration. Prompt confidentiality is out of scope: the broker never sees inference traffic and payload delivery is disabled.

status_legend.Mitigated: A control exists in code and is covered by tests.
status_legend.Accepted: Known residual risk, documented, not planned.
status_legend.Open: No control; listed so it is not forgotten.

boundaries.name: Application / end user -> broker
boundaries.crosses: OIDC JWT in X-Quota-User-Token; SigV4 on the AWS_IAM Function URL

boundaries.name: Broker -> STS / IAM
boundaries.crosses: AssumeRole with RoleSessionName = SourceIdentity = sanitized claim; inline session policy

boundaries.name: Vended session -> Bedrock
boundaries.crosses: IAM authorization of bedrock:InvokeModel*/CountTokens on allowed_model_arns; invocation log is the metering truth

boundaries.name: Invocation logs -> usage processor -> DynamoDB
boundaries.crosses: CloudWatch Logs subscription; identity.arn and modelId; transactional ledger writes

boundaries.name: DynamoDB streams -> enforcement processors -> IAM policy versions
boundaries.crosses: REVOCATION# sentinels, CONFIG#EMERGENCY_STOP; CreatePolicyVersion on pre-attached policies; PutRolePolicy on workload roles

boundaries.name: Admin UI / API -> admin mutations
boundaries.crosses: Shared admin key or admin JWT claim; separate break-glass key; If-Match + Idempotency-Key

boundaries.name: Operator / account administrator -> out-of-band IAM, SCP, logging

threats.title: JWT forgery or replay
threats.description: Attacker presents a fabricated or captured token to obtain credentials under another identity.
threats.mitigation: Signature verified against issuer JWKS (RS/ES) or dev-only HS256; iss/aud/exp enforced; discovery and JWKS must be HTTPS; lease deadline capped at token exp so a replayed token cannot mint credentials that outlive it.
threats.residual_risk: A token stolen before exp is usable until then; no jti replay cache. Caller must also hold a SigV4 principal allowed on the Function URL.

threats.title: jwt_user_claim user-controlled or IdP misconfigured
threats.description: If the quota claim is user-editable at the IdP, one user can spend another's budget.
threats.mitigation: Reserved prefixes and the workload: namespace are rejected; documentation directs operators to a stable IdP-controlled claim (default sub).
threats.residual_risk: IdP configuration is outside the sample.

threats.title: Vend flooding
threats.description: A client refreshes credentials in a loop, exhausting STS or DynamoDB.
threats.mitigation: Per-identity vend rate limit (VEND#<user>#<minute>, vend_rate_limit_per_minute) -> 429; logical lease refresh window rejects premature new lease IDs; Function URL requires a SigV4 principal from invoker_principal_arns.
threats.residual_risk: Many valid identities multiply the per-identity budget; SigV4 scopes who can try.

threats.title: Quota headers leak another user's state
threats.description: Response headers could expose limits of other subjects.
threats.mitigation: Headers describe only the authenticated identity's own limits.

threats.title: Session-name collision or injection
threats.description: Two identities sanitize to the same RoleSessionName, or a crafted claim escapes the session-name character set, so metering or revocation targets the wrong subject.
threats.mitigation: session_name_for derives a collision-resistant name (sanitized prefix + hash of the full claim) and the same value is SourceIdentity; the exact stamped value is persisted on the user row (source_identity) so revocation never re-derives it; SESSION# reverse map; SetSourceIdentity/TagSession granted only to the broker role on the trust policy.

threats.title: Session policy widens access
threats.description: The Resource:"*" in the lease session policy could grant models outside the allowlist.
threats.mitigation: STS intersects the session policy with the role policy and the permissions boundary; "*" only applies the DateLessThan deadline to the existing allowlist. Role grants exactly CountTokens, InvokeModel, InvokeModelWithResponseStream.

threats.title: Bearer-token bypass of the model allowlist
threats.description: bedrock:CallWithBearerToken requires Resource:"*" and would defeat the per-model ARN allowlist.
threats.mitigation: Not granted on the vended role, boundary, or session policy; DenyDirectBedrockPolicy and the SCP example explicitly deny it for other principals.

threats.title: bedrock-mantle endpoint bypass
threats.description: bedrock-mantle:CreateInference / CallWithBearerToken is a separate IAM service prefix and Bedrock Mantle calls are not captured by model-invocation logging; if reachable, spend is invisible to metering.
threats.mitigation: Verified: the vended role's identity policy, the permissions boundary, and the session policy grant only bedrock:* actions, so a vended session has no bedrock-mantle:* permission (denied by omission) and the boundary prevents adding it by editing the role alone.
threats.residual_risk: Other principals in the account with bedrock-mantle:* spend unmetered; DenyDirectBedrockPolicy and the SCP example should be extended with bedrock-mantle:CreateInference and bedrock-mantle:CallWithBearerToken where Mantle is not wanted. Documented in README 'Metering coverage caveat'.
threats.status_detail: Mitigated for vended sessions; Accepted (documented) for other principals

threats.title: requestMetadata spoofing
threats.description: The caller controls requestMetadata in the invocation log.
threats.mitigation: Never read for attribution; only identity.arn (Bedrock-populated) and modelId are used.

threats.title: Unmetered Runtime APIs
threats.description: StartAsyncInvoke and InvokeModelWithBidirectionalStream authorize under bedrock:InvokeModel* but produce no invocation-log record.
threats.mitigation: None possible in the data plane; documented with the recommendation to exclude such models from allowed_model_arns; listed as a reconciliation-delta cause.
threats.residual_risk: Spend through those APIs never reaches the ledger.

threats.title: Image generation priced at zero when image delivery is off
threats.description: A Nova Canvas record with imageDataDeliveryEnabled=false carries no token counts and no body, so images=0 and cost $0 with no missing_dimensions flag.
threats.mitigation: The record is still counted as a request (image-model heuristic prevents it being skipped as metadata-less) so volume is visible; README tells operators to enable image delivery or exclude image models.
threats.residual_risk: The one pricing gap the fallback alarm cannot detect.

threats.title: Invocation-log tampering or deletion by an account administrator
threats.description: logs:DeleteLogGroup or PutModelInvocationLoggingConfiguration removes or redirects the metering source.
threats.mitigation: Managed log group and logging configuration are RemovalPolicy.RETAIN; writer role trust is condition-scoped to aws:SourceAccount/aws:SourceArn. Opt-in reconciliation (reconciliation_enabled) is the detection control.
threats.residual_risk: An administrator can turn logging off; only detectable after the fact.

threats.title: Metering lag or stream lag leading to overspend
threats.description: Slow log delivery or a backed-up subscription delays detection.
threats.mitigation: Overspend bounded by construction: metering lag + min(lease remainder, deny propagation); lease deadline embedded in the credential and non-extending on retry; DetectionLagMilliseconds measured per record.
threats.residual_risk: Bound not measured under load (qualification pending); workload mode has no lease (T-19).

threats.title: Double-charging or lost increments on retry
threats.description: CloudWatch Logs delivery is at-least-once.
threats.mitigation: One TransactWriteItems with a conditional REQUEST#<id> marker Put plus subject and per-model ledger Updates; a cancelled transaction re-reads the marker before classifying as duplicate.

threats.title: Unresolved session -> usage silently lost
threats.description: A SESSION# map row expired so a late record cannot be attributed.
threats.mitigation: Logged as unresolved_sessions warning; retention floor 31 days; a session cannot outlive the vended STS credential (<= 3600 s).
threats.residual_risk: Only for records delivered days late.

threats.title: IAM eventual consistency
threats.description: CreatePolicyVersion succeeds but takes seconds to propagate; sessions keep working meanwhile.
threats.mitigation: Propagation is inside the documented bound; the lease is the fallback.
threats.residual_risk: Seconds of continued access after a block.

threats.title: Revocation shard overflow
threats.description: Blocking many identities fills a 6144-character shard; new identities in that shard are not IAM-cut.
threats.mitigation: Processor keeps the last-good deny set rather than clearing it; RevocationPolicyOverflowAlarm; lease still bounds new identities; shard count immutable to prevent rehash gaps.
threats.residual_risk: Capacity ~800-1100 simultaneously blocked identities; beyond that, new blocks rely on the lease.

threats.title: Enforcement processors escalate via IAM
threats.description: A compromised processor uses its IAM permissions to grant itself or the vended role wider access.
threats.mitigation: Revocation and emergency processors may only version their designated pre-attached policy ARNs (no AttachRolePolicy/CreatePolicy/role edits); the vended role's permissions boundary caps any policy version; workload enforcer PutRolePolicy scoped to exact configured role ARNs; emergency processor DynamoDB access restricted with dynamodb:LeadingKeys.

threats.title: Workload enforcement failure has no lease fallback
threats.description: A blocked workload keeps spending until PutRolePolicy succeeds; workload mode has no vend path and therefore no permission lease.
threats.mitigation: WorkloadEnforcementFailureAlarm; 5-minute repair schedule; manual attach procedure in the runbook.
threats.residual_risk: The only unbounded-overspend path in the system; alarmed.

threats.title: Stream consumer starvation
threats.description: A third users-table stream consumer would throttle the two enforcement readers.
threats.mitigation: Dispatcher fan-out design; synth test asserts exactly two EventSourceMappings.

threats.title: Admin key or emergency key exposure
threats.description: Leak of the routine or break-glass shared key.
threats.mitigation: Both keys in Secrets Manager, read at cold start, never sent to the browser (UI authorizes by admin JWT claim); break-glass key entered per action and not persisted; empty ADMIN_JWT_CLAIM disables JWT admin; both compares constant-time via secrets.compare_digest (the emergency compare was == until this review).
threats.residual_risk: Rotation is manual and needs container recycling.

threats.title: Admin JWT claim escalation at the IdP
threats.description: A user adds themselves to the admin group at the IdP.
threats.mitigation: Claim/value are operator-configured; IdP group membership is outside the sample.
threats.residual_risk: IdP governance.

threats.title: Unaudited or replayed administrative change
threats.description: An admin mutation without a durable record, or a replayed request applying twice.
threats.mitigation: Every create/limit/status/model-budget mutation writes an immutable audit event (actor, auth method, reason, before/after) and a request-hash-bound idempotency marker in the same transaction; If-Match versioning rejects lost updates; enforcement-dial and emergency actions write their own immutable audit rows.

threats.title: Authorized admin disables enforcement
threats.description: An admin makes every budget alert-only or Unlimited.
threats.mitigation: UI requires explicit confirmation and a reason for Unlimited, period changes, and alert-only thresholds; all changes audited.
threats.residual_risk: Cannot be prevented for a legitimate admin.

threats.title: Admin API returns CloudWatch/IAM internals
threats.description: Operations responses could leak secret ARNs or policy ARNs to the browser.
threats.mitigation: Operations exposes alarm keys/states, metric values, and configuration numbers only; never secret ARNs, policy ARNs, or the emergency key.

threats.title: Direct Bedrock access outside the vended role
threats.description: Any principal with bedrock:InvokeModel* (or bedrock-mantle:*) spends unmetered.
threats.mitigation: DenyDirectBedrockPolicyArn helper and SCP example; reconciliation detects the bill/ledger gap.
threats.residual_risk: The sample cannot constrain the management plane; production must apply the SCP/boundary.

threats.title: Administrator edits IAM, the boundary, the logging configuration, or DynamoDB directly
threats.description: Out-of-band changes to enforcement or ledger state.
threats.mitigation: None; RETAIN policies preserve evidence; CloudTrail (not deployed by this sample) is the audit source.
threats.residual_risk: Full.

threats.title: Price catalog manipulation
threats.description: An operator pins a $0 price to make a model free.
threats.mitigation: Synth requires a positive token pair except for image models with positive per_image, requires a reason on every override, and the catalog is reviewed in Git.
threats.residual_risk: Reviewed configuration, not a runtime control.

threats.title: Reconciliation reads the account bill
threats.description: With reconciliation_enabled a Lambda holds ce:GetCostAndUsage on * (no resource scoping exists) and stores account-level Bedrock USD as RECONCILE# rows in the usage table, readable through the admin API.
threats.mitigation: Opt-in, off by default; the grant is the single ce: verb and the function has no users/audit-table access; the CE query is filtered to Bedrock services and the stack Region and only totals are stored; the broker never calls CE and serves stored rows behind the same admin authorization as the ledger.
threats.residual_risk: An admin sees aggregate account Bedrock spend for the Region.

threats.title: Workload roster parameter
threats.description: The broker labels workload: rows and answers GET /admin/workloads from the WorkloadRosterParameter SSM parameter (name, model, inference-profile ARN, role ARN, enforcement_ready). ssm:PutParameter on it could relabel a role-less workload as Enforced or hide one from the console; reading it discloses role and profile ARNs.
threats.mitigation: Written only by CloudFormation; the broker grant is ssm:GetParameter on the single ARN; the roster is presentation only (the enforcer has its own copy and evaluates budgets from the ledger, so tampering cannot change what is enforced); POST /admin/users rejects the workload: namespace so no unregistered row can be minted through the API.
threats.residual_risk: A console label can mislead an admin in an account that is already compromised at the ssm:PutParameter level.

headline_accepts: The sample cannot constrain the account's management plane (T-12, T-26, T-27): apply the SCP.
Workload mode has no permission lease (T-19): an IAM failure there is the only unbounded-overspend path; it is alarmed.
